Real-World Object to Miniature Scale Converter

Another tool I built because I needed it myself

The reverse of my scale engine. Instead of converting between two miniature scales, it takes a real-world measurement — a wall, a dragon, a building — and converts it to the exact millimetre height at any tabletop scale. It uses the same 175cm human baseline with eyes at 160cm that powers every conversion on this site, so the numbers match the reference library and the scale engine exactly. No uploads, no accounts, no cookies.

Direct answer

Real-world height to miniature size

Convert the real measurement to millimetres, then multiply by (scale \u00F7 1600) for eye-level gaming scales, or divide by the ratio for 1:x scales. A 12-foot wall (3658mm) at 32mm scale is 73.2mm; at 1:56 it's 65.3mm. Same baseline as every other tool here — a 175cm human with eyes at 160cm.

A 28mm or 32mm column measures to eye level on the 175cm baseline; the 1:56 column is a strict ratio to the top of the head.

How to use the converter

  1. 1

    Measure the real thing

    Feet, inches, or centimetres — the converter accepts all three and syncs them as you type. For terrain and buildings, a tape measure on the real object is all you need.

  2. 2

    Pick the scale you're printing

    All 16 scales from the scale engine are here. Ratio scales measure to the top of the head; gaming scales measure to eye level — the converter switches automatically.

  3. 3

    Read the height and scale your STL

    The result is the height your print should be. If you already have a model, drop that number into the Slicer Percentage Calculator to get the exact percentage.

Real-World Scale Conversion FAQ

How tall is a 6-foot human in 28mm scale?

32mm. A 6-foot person is 1828.8mm tall; at 28mm scale on the 175cm baseline that converts to 1828.8 × (28 ÷ 1600) = 32mm — the same height a 32mm heroic miniature would be if it were true scale.

How do I convert feet and inches to millimetres?

One foot is exactly 304.8mm and one inch is 25.4mm. Multiply the total height in millimetres by (scale ÷ 1600) for gaming scales, or divide by the ratio for 1:x scales. The converter does this for you.

What baseline does this converter use?

A 175cm human with the eyes at 160cm — the same baseline as every conversion on this site. Gaming scales measure to eye level, ratio scales measure to the top of the head, and the converter handles both automatically.

How tall is a 12-foot wall in 32mm scale?

73.2mm. A 12-foot wall is 3658mm tall, and 3658 × (32 ÷ 1600) = 73.2mm — the default example the converter opens with. That is roughly a 3.7-inch wall for a skirmish table.

What is the difference between gaming scales and ratio scales?

Gaming scales like 28mm, 32mm, and 40mm are measured to eye level. Ratio scales like 1:35, 1:48, and 1:56 are a strict division of the 175cm human and measure to the top of the head.

How tall is a 2.1m door at tabletop scale?

At 28mm scale a 2100mm door is about 36.8mm — noticeably taller than a miniature, which is why terrain doorways are often oversized. At 32mm scale the same door is 42mm.
